subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — OTEL and Prometheus exporter mappings

question: Should OpenClaw standardize these six AI-safety event names and metrics as a core, plugin-visible contract, and if so may untrusted plugins contribute to the same operator-facing safety counters?
rationale: The answer determines a permanent plugin API, telemetry naming contract, producer ownership, and trust boundary; code review cannot safely infer that product and security policy.

options.title: Narrow and stage the contract
options.body: Approve only trusted core producers and exporter mappings now, while deferring plugin SDK exposure until provenance and compatibility rules are reviewed separately.

options.title: Approve the public taxonomy
options.body: Keep the plugin-visible contract but require explicit trusted/untrusted provenance, stable schema documentation, cardinality limits, and upgrade tests before merge.

options.title: Keep safety telemetry plugin-owned
options.body: Do not add this taxonomy to core and instead implement the optional safety telemetry model in a diagnostics or safety plugin.

recommendation.title: Narrow and stage the contract
recommendation.body: Approve only trusted core producers and exporter mappings now, while deferring plugin SDK exposure until provenance and compatibility rules are reviewed separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent diagnostics work defines the trusted-versus-plugin event boundary directly affected by this decision.
